title: Mailboxes
confirmDisconnect: Disconnect {email}? The emails and replies stored here will be deleted (your mailbox is not touched).
oauthIntro: No password is entered here: you grant access at Google or Microsoft (reading the inbox, drafts and sending).
oauthUnavailable: Not available: sign-in with this provider is not set up on this server ({prefix}_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET variables).
name: Name
tlsHint: Direct TLS: ports 993 (IMAP) and 465 (SMTP). Unchecked, the connection uses STARTTLS (143 / 587).
connected: Mailbox connected. Now choose the folder to watch.
chooseFolder: These are the folders of your own mailbox, as your mail provider lists them. Only the emails of the one you choose are fetched, as far back as you say below.
folderPending: An administrator has yet to choose the folder to watch.
intro: Each mailbox watches one folder. A shared mailbox is used by every member; only administrators connect, change or disconnect one.
step3: Try it on a first email
connectIntro: The emails of one folder that you choose are fetched, and your replies are sent from the same address. Nothing else in the mailbox is read.
mineHint: A personal mailbox. Only you see its emails; administrators have no access to it.
sharedHint: contact@, info@… Every member of {organization} sees its emails and can reply from it.
imapHint: With its address and a password (IMAP / SMTP).
passwordHint: The password is encrypted in the database. Prefer an application password.
connectHint: The connection is tested before anything is saved.
keyIntro: Sorting your emails and writing proposals go through OpenRouter, with your organisation’s own key. Without one you can still read and answer by hand.
keyHint: Create one in your <link>OpenRouter account</link>. It is encrypted in the database and used by every member who has no key of their own.
hostedSignIn: {address} is hosted at {provider}: connect it by signing in there, no password is typed here.
hostedPassword: {address} is hosted at {provider}, which usually refuses the mailbox’s own password. Use an application password, or ask whoever hosts this server to set up sign-in with {provider}.

servers.unknown: Your mail provider’s help lists them, as its IMAP and SMTP settings.
servers.searching: Looking for the mail servers of {domain}…
servers.found: Found for {domain}. Change them if your mail provider says otherwise.
servers.notFound: We could not find the mail servers of {domain}, and would rather not guess. Your mail provider’s help lists them, as its IMAP and SMTP settings.

fetchDays: {days, plural, one {the last day} other {the last # days}}
fetchBackHint: Read or not, unless you tick the box below. A fetch brings in the most recent first, a limited number at a time; what is already here stays.
unreadOnly: Only the emails I have not read yet in my mailbox
editIntro: The name its replies show, what is fetched from it, and how saras reaches it. Its address cannot be changed: connect the other one as a new mailbox.
nameHint: Shown beside the address on the replies sent from this mailbox. Empty, they show the address alone.
unreadOnlyShort: Only those not read yet in the mailbox
changeFetched: Change the folder or what is fetched
fetchedUnread: · {days, plural, one {last day} other {last # days}}, unread only
serversSaved: The mailbox answers there: saved. Fetching…
passwordKeptHint: Leave empty to keep the password saras already has. It is never shown.
